title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
description: Ten documented OSU study environments in Corvallis, spanning library nooks, lounges, cultural centers, and academic buildings.

cards.title: Valley Library Rotunda
cards.subtitle: Valley Library · Corvallis campus
cards.notes: Choose a rotunda nook on the second, fourth, or fifth floor for a compact solo setup; some nooks seat one person or a pair.
cards.short_summary: Multi-floor rotunda nooks provide small-scale seating inside the library.
cards.evidence_claim: OSU identifies seating nooks beside the Valley Library rotunda on the second, fourth, and fifth floors.
cards.access_notes: Use library access rules and current building hours; individual seating is not reservable.

cards.title: Memorial Union Student Lounge
cards.subtitle: Memorial Union · Corvallis campus
cards.notes: Set up at the large tables in the Memorial Union’s main-floor student lounge; move to the porch only when outdoor conditions suit.
cards.short_summary: A main-floor lounge with large tables and nearby JavaStop service.
cards.evidence_claim: OSU describes the Memorial Union’s main-floor student lounge as having large tables and notes JavaStop and its porch nearby.
cards.access_notes: Use current Memorial Union building access information; café purchases are optional and separate.

cards.title: Peavy Hall Upper-Floor Seating
cards.subtitle: Peavy Hall · Corvallis campus
cards.notes: Head upstairs for the row of high-backed chairs by floor-to-ceiling windows, then use the natural light for reading or laptop work.
cards.short_summary: High-backed window chairs offer an indoor reading-and-writing setting.
cards.evidence_claim: OSU directs students upstairs in Peavy Hall to high-backed chairs paired with floor-to-ceiling windows.
cards.access_notes: Use current Peavy Hall building access information before planning a session.

cards.title: International Living-Learning Center Common Area
cards.subtitle: International Living-Learning Center · Corvallis campus
cards.notes: Bring work that tolerates ambient conversation and use the ILLC common area; Cascadia Café or Market is nearby if you need a break.
cards.short_summary: A common-area environment suited to work with background activity.
cards.evidence_claim: OSU describes the International Living-Learning Center as a study setting with ambient conversation and Cascadia Café or Market steps away.
cards.access_notes: Use current ILLC building access information; food and drinks require separate purchase.

cards.title: Learning Innovation Center Top-Floor Seating
cards.subtitle: Learning Innovation Center · Corvallis campus
cards.notes: Take readings or a project to the upper floors, and look for a fifth-floor seat facing Marys Peak when one is available.
cards.short_summary: Upper-floor seating pairs project work with broad valley-facing views.
cards.evidence_claim: OSU highlights top-floor Learning Innovation Center study seating, including fifth-floor views toward Marys Peak.
cards.access_notes: Use current Learning Innovation Center building access information; seating is not described as reservable.

cards.title: Austin Hall Fireplace Seating
cards.subtitle: Austin Hall · Corvallis campus
cards.notes: Choose a couch with a fireplace view or a café table by the windows, then keep food and drink purchases separate from your study plan.
cards.short_summary: Fireplace-side couches and window tables provide two work setups in Austin Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: OSU identifies fireplace-view couches and window-side café tables in Austin Hall as study options.
cards.access_notes: Use current Austin Hall building access information; Trader Bing’s purchases are separate.

cards.title: Champinefu Lodge Basic Needs Center
cards.subtitle: Champinefu Lodge · Corvallis campus
cards.notes: If you are an OSU student, use the Basic Needs Center’s fireplace-side seating; its beverage station and microwave support a longer session.
cards.short_summary: A student-accessible center with fireplace seating and basic food-prep amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: OSU states that Champinefu Lodge houses the Basic Needs Center, open to all students, with a fireplace, beverage station, and microwave.
cards.access_notes: Open to OSU students; confirm the Basic Needs Center’s current access information before visiting.

cards.title: Women’s Building Lobby
cards.subtitle: Women’s Building · Corvallis campus
cards.notes: Use the lobby’s high-backed chairs and fireplace for independent work, and bring headphones in case an adjacent gym class is active.
cards.short_summary: A historic lobby workspace with high-backed chairs and a fireplace.
cards.evidence_claim: OSU describes the Women’s Building lobby as having wood floors, high-backed chairs, and a fireplace, with occasional adjacent gym classes.
cards.access_notes: Use current Women’s Building access information; noise from the adjacent gym may vary.

cards.entity_name: SLUG Honors College Student Learning Center
cards.title: SLUG Honors College Student Learning Center
cards.subtitle: Learning Innovation Center 340 · Honors College
cards.notes: Honors College students can use the tables, writable surfaces, computers, and lounge; contact the college if a private study room is needed.
cards.short_summary: An Honors College learning center with study tools and a reservable private room.
cards.evidence_claim: OSU lists computers, free printing, study and lounge space, writable surfaces, and a private study room at the SLUG in LInC 340.
cards.access_notes: The SLUG is the Honors College student learning space; contact Honors College to reserve its study room.

cards.title: Ettihad Cultural Center Study Spaces
cards.subtitle: Student Experience Center Suite 380
cards.notes: Use the center’s study or quiet space, then switch to its computers or mini library when your work calls for a different setup.
cards.short_summary: A Student Experience Center cultural-resource space with study and quiet areas.
cards.evidence_claim: OSU lists study spaces, a quiet space, computers, and a mini library among Ettihad Cultural Center resources.
cards.access_notes: OSU says the center’s space and resources are open to students, faculty, staff, and the wider OSU community.
